entries.label: Tool versions
entries.description: Docker server version and architecture, Compose, kind, kubectl, helm (optional).
entries.command: docker version --format 'docker {{.Server.Version}} {{.Server.Arch}}'; docker compose version --short; kind version; kubectl version --client; helm version --short

entries.label: Docker resources
entries.description: CPUs and memory available to containers: 4 CPUs and 8 GB minimum, 12 GB for Lab 4.
entries.command: docker info --format '{{.NCPU}} CPUs, {{.MemTotal}} bytes of memory'

entries.label: Run the preflight check
entries.description: Tools, engine, free ports and Docker Hub access; every line should be PASS.
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab00/preflight.sh

entries.label: Pull the lab images
entries.description: Pulls the six pinned images; ends with done.
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab00/pull-images.sh

entries.label: Smoke test the RabbitMQ image
entries.description: Should print 4.3.7.
entries.command: docker run --rm rabbitmq:4.3.7-management rabbitmq-diagnostics --version

entries.label: Which lab images are present
entries.description: Lists the pinned images found locally (six expected).
entries.command: docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}' | grep -xE 'rabbitmq:(4\.3\.7|3\.13\.7)-management|pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2\.25\.0|prom/prometheus:v3\.7\.3|grafana/grafana:12\.2\.1|python:3\.13-alpine'

entries.label: Who holds a port
entries.description: Shows the process listening on 15672 (change the port as needed).
entries.command: lsof -nP -iTCP:15672 -sTCP:LISTEN

entries.label: All lab containers
entries.description: Every caci- container with its status and ports.
entries.command: docker ps -a --filter name=caci- --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}'

entries.label: Lab 1/2: start the single node
entries.description: One RabbitMQ 4.3.7 node, caci-rmq on caci-net; waits until healthy.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab01/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 1/2: status
entries.description: The caci-single project's container.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab01/docker-compose.yml ps

entries.label: Lab 1/2: stop
entries.description: ⚠ Removes the node and its volume (all queues and messages).
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab01/docker-compose.yml down -v

entries.label: Lab 3: start the three-node cluster
entries.description: caci-rmq1..3, cluster caci-lab, UIs on 15672–15674.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab03/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 5: start the cluster plus Prometheus and Grafana
entries.description: Adds caci-prometheus (9090) and caci-grafana (3000) to the Lab 3 cluster.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab05/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 6: start everything plus the DR site
entries.description: Adds caci-rmq-dr (UI 15675) to the Lab 5 stack.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab06/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 6: declare the order flow
entries.description: orders.events with orders.billing and orders.billing.dr-copy on the primary; prints primary topology ready.
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab06/setup-topology.sh

entries.label: Lab 3/5/6: status
entries.description: Every container of the caci-lab Compose project.
entries.command: docker compose -p caci-lab ps --format 'table {{.Name}}\t{{.Status}}'

entries.label: Lab 3/5/6: stop
entries.description: ⚠ Removes the cluster, DR site, Prometheus, Grafana and their volumes.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab06/docker-compose.yml down -v --remove-orphans

entries.label: Lab 7: start blue (3.13) and green (4.3)
entries.description: Six brokers on caci-l7-net; UIs blue 15701, green 15711.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab07/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 7: build the blue legacy estate
entries.description: Mirrored classic queues, a lazy queue, users boomi-a/b/c; prints blue legacy estate ready.
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab07/blue-setup.sh

entries.label: Lab 7: status
entries.description: Brokers and stand-in processes of the caci-lab7 project.
entries.command: docker ps -a --filter name=caci-l7- --format 'table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}'

entries.label: Lab 7: stop
entries.description: ⚠ Removes the stand-in processes, both clusters, their volumes and the exported definition files.
entries.command: docker rm -fv $(docker ps -aq --filter name=caci-l7-) >/dev/null 2>&1; docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab07/docker-compose.yml down -v --remove-orphans; rm -f ../labs/files/lab07/blue-definitions.json ../labs/files/lab07/green-definitions.json ../labs/files/lab07/blue-final-definitions.json

entries.label: Lab 8: start the 4.3 broker
entries.description: caci-l8-rmq on caci-l8-net, UI 15681; can run beside any other lab.
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab08/docker-compose.yml up -d --wait

entries.label: Lab 8: start the optional 3.13 broker
entries.description: caci-l8-rmq313, UI 15682 (profile v313, Step 8).
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab08/docker-compose.yml --profile v313 up -d --wait rmq313

entries.label: Lab 8: declare boomi.orders
entries.description: The quorum queue the stand-in Molecule consumes.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare queue --name boomi.orders --type quorum --durable true

entries.label: Lab 8: stop
entries.description: ⚠ Removes the stand-ins, both brokers and their volumes.
entries.command: for c in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter name=caci-l8- | grep -v -- '-rmq'); do docker rm -f "$c"; done; docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab08/docker-compose.yml --profile v313 down -v

entries.label: Lab 4: create the kind cluster
entries.description: caci-k8s: one control plane, four workers labelled ahv-host-a/a/b/c.
entries.command: kind create cluster --config ../labs/files/lab04/kind-config.yaml

entries.label: Lab 4: load images into kind
entries.description: Copies rabbitmq:4.3.7-management and perf-test:2.25.0 into the nodes (slow or filtered networks).
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab04/load-images.sh

entries.label: Lab 4: install cert-manager
entries.description: v1.21.3, then waits for its deployments.
entries.command: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.21.3/cert-manager.yaml && kubectl -n cert-manager wait --for=condition=Available deploy --all --timeout=300s

entries.label: Lab 4: install the Cluster Operator
entries.description: v2.23.1 in rabbitmq-system.
entries.command: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/rabbitmq/cluster-operator/releases/download/v2.23.1/cluster-operator.yml && kubectl -n rabbitmq-system wait --for=condition=Available deploy --all --timeout=300s

entries.label: Lab 4: install the Messaging Topology Operator
entries.description: v1.20.4 (needs cert-manager).
entries.command: kubectl apply -f https://github.com/rabbitmq/messaging-topology-operator/releases/download/v1.20.4/messaging-topology-operator-with-certmanager.yaml && kubectl -n rabbitmq-system wait --for=condition=Available deploy --all --timeout=300s

entries.label: Lab 4: deploy RabbitmqCluster caci-rabbit
entries.description: Namespace messaging, three pods spread over three AHV hosts.
entries.command: kubectl create namespace messaging; kubectl apply -f ../labs/files/lab04/rabbitmq-cluster.yaml

entries.label: Lab 4: wait for the cluster
entries.description: condition met after 2–4 minutes.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging wait --for=condition=AllReplicasReady rabbitmqcluster/caci-rabbit --timeout=600s

entries.label: Lab 4: apply the PDB and the topology
entries.description: PodDisruptionBudget caci-rabbit, then vhost, exchange, queue, binding, policy, user and permission objects.
entries.command: kubectl apply -f ../labs/files/lab04/pdb.yaml -f ../labs/files/lab04/topology.yaml

entries.label: Lab 4: delete the kind cluster
entries.description: ⚠ Removes caci-k8s with every object and volume in it.
entries.command: kind delete cluster --name caci-k8s

entries.label: Version and Erlang
entries.description: RabbitMQ 4.3.7 on Erlang/OTP 27.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q status | grep -E 'RabbitMQ version|Erlang configuration'

entries.label: Full node status
entries.description: Memory, alarms, listeners, file descriptors, disk limit, uptime.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q status

entries.label: Server version
entries.description: Just the version string of the running node.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q server_version

entries.label: Node is running
entries.description: fully booted and running; the readiness check.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_running

entries.label: All three nodes running
entries.description: check_running on every node of the Lab 3 cluster.
entries.command: for n in 1 2 3; do docker exec caci-rmq$n rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_running; done

entries.label: Local alarms
entries.description: reported no local alarms; in 4.3.7 it passed even with a memory or disk alarm on the node: use check_alarms too.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_local_alarms

entries.label: Cluster-wide alarms check
entries.description: Fails if any node in the cluster has an alarm.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_alarms

entries.label: List alarms
entries.description: Memory or free disk alarms, local and cluster-wide.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q alarms

entries.label: Listener ports respond
entries.description: Connects to every listener (AMQP, HTTP, Prometheus); the Compose healthcheck of Lab 1.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_port_connectivity

entries.label: Listeners
entries.description: Which ports and protocols the node serves.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q listeners

entries.label: Memory breakdown
entries.description: Where memory goes: queues, connections, binaries, metadata (MB).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q memory_breakdown --unit mb | head -12

entries.label: Overview via the HTTP API
entries.description: rabbitmqadmin v2 summary: version, cluster, totals and rates (Lab 1 node).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab show overview

entries.label: Deprecated features in use
entries.description: Non-zero exit while a deprecated feature is used; on Lab 7 blue it lists classic_queue_mirroring.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmq-diagnostics check_if_any_deprecated_features_are_used

entries.label: Alarm and memory log lines
entries.description: Last alarm/memory messages from rmq2's log (after an alarm drill).
entries.command: docker logs --since 10m caci-rmq2 2>&1 | grep -iE 'alarm|memory' | tail -5

entries.label: Deprecation warnings in the log
entries.description: management_metrics_collection is deprecated: Prometheus is the supported monitoring path.
entries.command: docker logs caci-rmq1 2>&1 | grep -i deprecated | head -3

entries.label: Cluster status
entries.description: Cluster name, disk and running nodes, versions, maintenance status, alarms.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl cluster_status

entries.label: Running nodes
entries.description: Only the Running Nodes section; compare from both sides during a partition.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl cluster_status | sed -n '/Running Nodes/,/Versions/p'

entries.label: Maintenance status
entries.description: not under maintenance / marked for maintenance per node.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl cluster_status | sed -n '/Maintenance status/,/Alarms/p'

entries.label: Declare the quorum queue orders
entries.description: Lab 3's demo queue on the cluster.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare queue --name orders --type quorum --durable true

entries.label: Quorum status of orders
entries.description: One row per member: leader/follower, voter, log and commit index, term.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-queues quorum_status orders

entries.label: Queues with leader, members, online
entries.description: A queue whose online list is shorter than members is missing a replica.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl -q list_queues name type leader members online messages

entries.label: Leaders per node
entries.description: How many quorum queue leaders each node holds.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl -q list_queues --no-table-headers leader | sort | uniq -c

entries.label: Is rmq2 quorum-critical?
entries.description: no queues/streams with minimum quorum means rmq2 can go down safely.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-queues check_if_node_is_quorum_critical

entries.label: Rebalance quorum leaders
entries.description: Spreads leaders evenly after restarts.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-queues rebalance quorum

entries.label: Grow quorum queues onto a node
entries.description: Adds a member on rmq3 to every quorum queue that lacks one (after a node replacement or scale-up).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmq-queues grow rabbit@rmq3 all

entries.label: Declare the order exchanges
entries.description: orders.direct, orders.events (topic), orders.broadcast (fanout) in vhost integration.
entries.command: for x in orders.direct:direct orders.events:topic orders.broadcast:fanout; do docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare exchange -V integration --name "${x%%:*}" --type "${x#*:}" --durable true; done

entries.label: Declare the order queues
entries.description: orders.billing, orders.shipping, orders.audit as quorum queues.
entries.command: for q in orders.billing orders.shipping orders.audit; do docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare queue -V integration --name $q --type quorum --durable true; done

entries.label: Bind a queue
entries.description: orders.events → orders.audit with order.# (quote topic patterns).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare binding -V integration --source orders.events --destination-type queue --destination orders.audit --routing-key 'order.#'

entries.label: Queues in vhost integration
entries.description: Name, type, durability and depth.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_queues -q -p integration name type durable messages

entries.label: Exchanges in vhost integration
entries.description: Name and type, including the built-in amq.* exchanges.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_exchanges -q -p integration name type durable

entries.label: Bindings in vhost integration
entries.description: Source exchange, destination queue, routing key.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_bindings -q -p integration source_name destination_name routing_key

entries.label: Queue depth and consumers
entries.description: Ready, unacked and consumers per queue on the cluster.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_queues -q name type messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers

entries.label: Lab 8 queue view
entries.description: Ready, unacked, consumers and consumer capacity (empty for quorum queues).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqctl -q list_queues name type messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers consumer_capacity

entries.label: Broker rates for a queue
entries.description: Publish, deliver, ack and redeliver rates of boomi.orders (5-second average, HTTP API).
entries.command: curl -s -u admin:caci-lab 'http://localhost:15681/api/queues/%2F/boomi.orders' | grep -oE '"(publish|deliver_get|ack|redeliver)_details":\{"rate":[0-9.]+' | sed -E 's/"([a-z_]+)_details":\{"rate":/\1 /' | tr '\n' ' '; echo

entries.label: Consumers: prefetch and acks
entries.description: prefetch_count 0 means unlimited: a consumer may hoard the queue.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_consumers -q queue_name prefetch_count ack_required

entries.label: Consumers: single active consumer
entries.description: active and activity_status: one single_active, the rest waiting (Lab 8 boomi.sac).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqctl -q list_consumers queue_name channel_pid prefetch_count active activity_status

entries.label: Connections and their state
entries.description: blocked = publishing during an alarm; blocking = will block on its next publish.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_connections -q name user state

entries.label: Connection states counted
entries.description: A quick view of running / blocked / blocking connections.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_connections -s state | sort | uniq -c

entries.label: Connections per node
entries.description: Which node holds the clients (pick a node to kill in Lab 6).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_connections -q --no-table-headers pid | sed -E 's/^<([^.]*)\..*/\1/' | sort | uniq -c

entries.label: Negotiated frame_max and channels
entries.description: frame_max 131072 is the default; lower values cost CPU on large messages.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_connections -q name user frame_max channels

entries.label: Channels
entries.description: Per channel: consumers, unacked messages, prefetch.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_channels -q connection number consumer_count messages_unacknowledged prefetch_count

entries.label: Delete a queue
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes lab.batch and its messages (Lab 5 cleanup; change the name).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl delete_queue lab.batch

entries.label: Create vhost integration
entries.description: Default queue type quorum (Lab 1).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare vhost --name integration --default-queue-type quorum --description "Order integration"

entries.label: Grant admin on integration
entries.description: Full configure/write/read for admin in the new vhost.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare permissions -V integration --username admin --configure '.*' --read '.*' --write '.*'

entries.label: List vhosts
entries.description: Name, default queue type, description.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab list vhosts

entries.label: Least-privilege user boomi-orders
entries.description: No tags: no management UI or API access.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare user --name boomi-orders --password 'Orders-Lab-2026' --tags ''

entries.label: Permissions for boomi-orders
entries.description: Configure nothing, write the two order exchanges, read billing and shipping.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare permissions -V integration --username boomi-orders --configure '^$' --write '^orders\.(direct|events)$' --read '^orders\.(billing|shipping)$'

entries.label: Users and permissions
entries.description: Users with tags, then every user's permissions in integration.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_users -q; docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqctl list_permissions -q -p integration

entries.label: API refuses a user without tags
entries.description: Expect {"error":"not_authorised","reason":"Not management user"}.
entries.command: curl -s -u boomi-orders:Orders-Lab-2026 http://localhost:15672/api/overview

entries.label: Alternate-exchange policy
entries.description: Unroutable messages from orders.direct go to orders.unrouted (create that exchange and queue first, Lab 1 Step 8).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare policy -V integration --name orders-ae --pattern '^orders\.direct$' --apply-to exchanges --definition '{"alternate-exchange":"orders.unrouted"}'

entries.label: DLX and delivery-limit policy
entries.description: orders-dlx on the cluster: dead-letter to dlx after 5 failed deliveries.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare policy --name orders-dlx --pattern '^orders$' --apply-to quorum_queues --definition '{"dead-letter-exchange":"dlx","delivery-limit":5}'

entries.label: Operator policy guardrails
entries.description: max-length 100000 and delivery-limit 10 on every queue; the lower value wins when both set one.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare operator_policy --name guardrails --pattern '.*' --apply-to queues --definition '{"max-length":100000,"delivery-limit":10}'

entries.label: List policies and operator policies
entries.description: Both kinds in vhost /.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_policies -q; docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_operator_policies -q

entries.label: Effective policy per queue
entries.description: Policy, operator policy and the merged definition.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_queues -q name policy operator_policy effective_policy_definition

entries.label: Remove the guardrails operator policy
entries.description: Clears the Lab 3 operator policy.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl clear_operator_policy guardrails

entries.label: Limit connections on vhost /
entries.description: ⚠ max-connections 20: further connections are refused (Lab 6 Scenario 6).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl set_vhost_limits -p / '{"max-connections": 20}'

entries.label: Show vhost limits
entries.description: Current limits of every vhost.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_vhost_limits --global

entries.label: Clear vhost limits
entries.description: Removes the connection limit on /.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl clear_vhost_limits -p /

entries.label: Publish to an exchange
entries.description: orders.direct, key created (Lab 1); prints whether it was routed.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab publish message -V integration -e orders.direct -k created -m '{"order":4711}'

entries.label: Publish through the HTTP API
entries.description: curl publish to orders.events; expect {"routed":true}.
entries.command: curl -s -u admin:caci-lab -H 'content-type: application/json' -X POST http://localhost:15672/api/exchanges/integration/orders.events/publish -d '{"properties":{"delivery_mode":2,"content_type":"application/json"},"routing_key":"order.us.created","payload":"{\"order\":4713}","payload_encoding":"string"}'

entries.label: Publish five poison messages
entries.description: bad-1..5 to boomi.poison through the default exchange (Lab 8).
entries.command: for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab publish message -k boomi.poison -m "bad-$i"; done

entries.label: Peek at a message
entries.description: Gets one and puts it back (ack_requeue_true): payload, redelivered, exchange, key.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab get messages -V integration -q orders.billing -c 1 -a ack_requeue_true

entries.label: Reject with requeue
entries.description: Each reject counts as a failed delivery toward delivery-limit (Lab 8 boomi.poison).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab get messages -q boomi.poison -c 5 -a reject_requeue_true --table-style psql

entries.label: Take a message off the queue
entries.description: ⚠ Gets one message and acknowledges it: it is removed.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab get messages -V integration -q orders.unrouted -c 1 -a ack_requeue_false

entries.label: Inspect the DLQ (x-death)
entries.description: One dead-lettered message, put back: look for x-death reason delivery_limit and x-delivery-count.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab get messages -q boomi.dlq -c 1 -a ack_requeue_true --table-style psql | cut -c1-600

entries.label: DLQ headers via the HTTP API
entries.description: x-first-death-queue/-reason and x-delivery-count of one boomi.dlq message, requeued.
entries.command: curl -s -u admin:caci-lab -H 'content-type: application/json' -X POST 'http://localhost:15681/api/queues/%2F/boomi.dlq/get' -d '{"count":1,"ackmode":"ack_requeue_true","encoding":"auto"}' | grep -oE '"x-(death|delivery-count|first-death-queue|first-death-reason)":(\[[^]]*\]|[^,]*)'

entries.label: Purge a queue (rabbitmqadmin)
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes every ready message in orders.billing (Lab 6 DR drill).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab purge queue --name orders.billing

entries.label: Purge a queue (rabbitmqctl)
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes every ready message in boomi.orders (Lab 8).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqctl -q purge_queue boomi.orders

entries.label: 3.13: declare boomi.poison
entries.description: Quorum queue on the Lab 8 3.13 broker via the HTTP API (its image has no rabbitmqadmin v2).
entries.command: curl -s -u admin:caci-lab -H 'content-type: application/json' -X PUT 'http://localhost:15682/api/queues/%2F/boomi.poison' -d '{"durable":true,"arguments":{"x-queue-type":"quorum"}}'

entries.label: 3.13: publish three poison messages
entries.description: Expect three {"routed":true}.
entries.command: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -u admin:caci-lab -H 'content-type: application/json' -X POST 'http://localhost:15682/api/exchanges/%2F/amq.default/publish' -d "{\"properties\":{},\"routing_key\":\"boomi.poison\",\"payload\":\"bad-$i\",\"payload_encoding\":\"string\"}"; echo; done

entries.label: 3.13: delivery count after a nack loop
entries.description: On 3.13 nacks count: x-delivery-count in the hundreds or thousands, and no default limit.
entries.command: curl -s -u admin:caci-lab -H 'content-type: application/json' -X POST 'http://localhost:15682/api/queues/%2F/boomi.poison/get' -d '{"count":3,"ackmode":"reject_requeue_true","encoding":"auto"}' | grep -o '"x-delivery-count":[0-9]*' | head -1

entries.label: Wait for quorum plus one
entries.description: Returns when every quorum queue on rmq2 has enough other members online (what the operator's preStop runs).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-upgrade await_online_quorum_plus_one -t 120

entries.label: Drain rmq2
entries.description: ⚠ Maintenance mode: moves rmq2's leaders away, closes its client connections, refuses new ones.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-upgrade drain

entries.label: Revive rmq2
entries.description: Takes rmq2 out of maintenance mode without a restart.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-upgrade revive

entries.label: Restart rmq2
entries.description: ⚠ Restarts the container; a restart also resets maintenance mode.
entries.command: docker restart caci-rmq2

entries.label: Wait until rmq2 is running
entries.description: Polls check_running every 2 s, then prints up.
entries.command: until docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_running >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done; echo up

entries.label: Maintenance lines in the log
entries.description: Marked for maintenance, ready to shut down, resetting maintenance status.
entries.command: docker logs --since 5m caci-rmq2 2>&1 | grep -i maintenance

entries.label: Feature flags
entries.description: Name and state of every feature flag.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl -q list_feature_flags name state

entries.label: Feature flags not enabled (blue)
entries.description: Before an upgrade: only the experimental khepri_db may stay disabled on 3.13.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmqctl -q list_feature_flags name state | grep -v enabled

entries.label: Enable all stable feature flags
entries.description: Required before upgrading to the next minor version.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl enable_feature_flag all

entries.label: Export definitions (Lab 1)
entries.description: Vhosts, users (hashed passwords), permissions, exchanges, queues, bindings, policies into lab01.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab definitions export --stdout > ../labs/files/lab01/integration-definitions.json && grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' ../labs/files/lab01/integration-definitions.json | sort -u

entries.label: Export definitions with rabbitmqctl
entries.description: Blue's complete topology to lab07/blue-definitions.json (Lab 7 Step 3).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmqctl -q export_definitions - > ../labs/files/lab07/blue-definitions.json

entries.label: Memory alarm on rmq2
entries.description: ⚠ Watermark 50MB: blocks every publisher in the cluster.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmqctl set_vm_memory_high_watermark absolute 50MB

entries.label: Restore the memory watermark
entries.description: Back to 0.6 of available memory; connections return to running.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmqctl set_vm_memory_high_watermark 0.6

entries.label: Disk alarm on rmq1
entries.description: ⚠ Free-disk limit 5000GB: the node thinks the disk is full and blocks publishers.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl set_disk_free_limit 5000GB

entries.label: Restore the disk limit
entries.description: Back to 1GB; the check runs every few seconds.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl set_disk_free_limit 1GB

entries.label: Stop the leader node
entries.description: ⚠ Graceful stop of rmq1; a new leader is elected within seconds.
entries.command: docker stop caci-rmq1

entries.label: Stop a second node
entries.description: ⚠ rmq3 too: one of three left, no majority, writes refused.
entries.command: docker stop caci-rmq3

entries.label: Publish without a majority
entries.description: Hangs about 30 s, then errors; the message may still be committed later (duplicate).
entries.command: time docker exec caci-rmq2 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab publish message -k orders -m during-outage

entries.label: Start the stopped nodes
entries.description: rmq1 and rmq3 rejoin; give them about 25 s.
entries.command: docker start caci-rmq1 caci-rmq3

entries.label: Crash a node
entries.description: ⚠ docker kill (no clean shutdown) of rmq3.
entries.command: docker kill caci-rmq3

entries.label: Partition rmq3
entries.description: ⚠ Disconnects rmq3 from caci-net while it keeps running: it becomes a minority.
entries.command: docker network disconnect caci-net caci-rmq3

entries.label: Heal the partition
entries.description: Reconnects rmq3 with its rmq3 and rabbitmq DNS aliases.
entries.command: docker network connect --alias rmq3 --alias rabbitmq caci-net caci-rmq3

entries.label: Running nodes as rmq3 sees them
entries.description: During a partition rmq3 lists only itself.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq3 rabbitmq-diagnostics -q cluster_status | sed -n '/Running Nodes/,/Versions/p'

entries.label: E1: fire and forget
entries.description: Classic queue, no confirms, auto-ack: fast and unsafe.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e1 --auto-delete true --producers 1 --consumers 1 --autoack 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E2: classic, confirms 100, manual acks
entries.description: The reliability contract on a classic queue, prefetch 100.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e2 --auto-delete true --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 100 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E3: quorum, confirms 100
entries.description: Replication and fsync: about half of E2.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e3 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 100 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E4: quorum, confirm 1
entries.description: Waiting for each confirm: a small fraction of E3.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e4 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 1 --qos 100 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E5: prefetch 1
entries.description: Receive rate collapses: one round trip per message.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e5 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 1 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E6: prefetch 50
entries.description: Compare the receiving rate with E5.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e6 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 50 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E7: 1 KB messages
entries.description: Message size baseline.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e7 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 100 --size 1000 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E8: 100 KB messages
entries.description: More bytes per second, far fewer messages.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --time 15 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.e8 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --confirm 100 --qos 100 --size 100000 2>&1 | grep -E 'rate avg|latency min'

entries.label: E9: one slow consumer
entries.description: 600 msg/s in, one consumer at 5 ms per message: the queue grows (Little's Law).
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue lab.e9 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 1 --rate 600 --confirm 100 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 5000 --time 20 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'rate avg'

entries.label: E10: six slow consumers
entries.description: Same work per message, six consumers keep up.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue lab.e10 --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 6 --rate 600 --confirm 100 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 5000 --time 20 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'rate avg'

entries.label: Background clients to inspect
entries.description: caci-pt-bg: 1 producer, 2 consumers for 25 s; inspect connections and consumers meanwhile.
entries.command: docker run -d --rm --name caci-pt-bg --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue lab.bg --producers 1 --consumers 2 --rate 100 --time 25

entries.label: Publish as boomi-orders
entries.description: 100 messages over AMQP as the least-privilege user; a sending rate line means allowed.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri 'amqp://boomi-orders:Orders-Lab-2026@rmq/integration' --exchange orders.direct --type direct --routing-key created --predeclared --skip-binding-queues --queue orders.billing --producers 1 --consumers 0 --pmessages 100 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'sending rate'

entries.label: boomi-orders may not declare
entries.description: Expect reply-code=403 ACCESS_REFUSED (configure '^$').
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri 'amqp://boomi-orders:Orders-Lab-2026@rmq/integration' --queue my.own.queue --producers 1 --consumers 0 --pmessages 1 2>&1 | grep -o 'reply-code=403, reply-text=[^,]*' | head -1

entries.label: Poison loop with basic.nack (Lab 2)
entries.description: Since 4.3 nack-requeue does not count toward delivery-limit: thousands/s for 5 messages.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue lab.poison --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 1 --nack --time 8 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'receiving rate'

entries.label: Load 5000 messages into orders
entries.description: Lab 3 cluster: then compare commit indexes in quorum_status.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --queue orders --predeclared --producers 1 --consumers 0 --pmessages 5000 --confirm 100 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'sending rate'

entries.label: Backlog with no consumers (Lab 5)
entries.description: caci-backlog: 300 msg/s to lab.backlog for 10 min; fires the backlog and no-consumer alerts.
entries.command: docker run -d --rm --name caci-backlog --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --queue lab.backlog --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 300 --confirm 100 --confirm-timeout 600 --time 600 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Four backlogs: expected batch
entries.description: caci-l5-batch-sub/-pub: 12,000 messages at once, two healthy consumers work through them.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l5-batch-sub --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.batch --quorum-queue --producers 0 --consumers 2 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 10000; docker run -d --name caci-l5-batch-pub --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.batch --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 2000 --pmessages 12000 --confirm 100

entries.label: Four backlogs: missing consumer
entries.description: caci-l5-nocons: 50 msg/s and nobody consuming.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l5-nocons --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.nocons --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 50 --confirm 50

entries.label: Four backlogs: slow downstream
entries.description: caci-l5-slow: 100 msg/s, two consumers at 100 ms per message.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l5-slow --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1 --metrics-format compact --queue lab.slow --quorum-queue --producers 1 --consumers 2 --qos 10 --rate 100 --consumer-latency 100000 --confirm 50

entries.label: Lab 6 steady traffic
entries.description: (Re)starts caci-traffic: 300 msg/s through orders.events into orders.billing, via the shared name rabbitmq.
entries.command: docker rm -f caci-traffic >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run -d --name caci-traffic --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rabbitmq --exchange orders.events --type topic --routing-key order.us.created --predeclared --skip-binding-queues --queue orders.billing --producers 1 --consumers 1 --rate 300 --confirm 50 --qos 50 --time 1800 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Lab 6 traffic, last 20 seconds
entries.description: Sent, confirmed, received per second; gaps show what clients saw.
entries.command: docker logs --tail 20 caci-traffic 2>&1 | grep 'msg/s' | grep -v 'rate avg' | awk '{print $2, "sent", $3, "confirmed", $5, "received", $9}'

entries.label: Lab 6 poison consumer
entries.description: caci-poison: nack-requeue loop on orders.poison for 5 min; fires RabbitMQRedeliveryLoop.
entries.command: docker run -d --rm --name caci-poison --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rabbitmq --queue orders.poison --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 1 --nack --time 300 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Connection storm
entries.description: 30 connections against a limit of 20: expect connection limit (20) is reached.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rabbitmq --queue lab.storm --producers 30 --consumers 0 --rate 1 --time 5 2>&1 | grep -o 'reply-text=[^,]*' | sort | uniq -c

entries.label: Lab 8 feed 200 msg/s
entries.description: caci-l8-feed: a stand-in Boomi Send process, persistent messages with confirms.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l8-feed --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.orders --predeclared --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 200 --confirm 50 --flag persistent --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Molecule: 3 nodes × 2 consumers, 20 ms
entries.description: caci-l8-node1..3, prefetch 10: 6 consumers, unacked ceiling 60, keeps up.
entries.command: for i in 1 2 3; do docker run -d --name caci-l8-node$i --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.orders --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 2 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 20000 --metrics-format compact; done

entries.label: Molecule with a slow downstream
entries.description: 3 × 2 consumers at 100 ms: unacked pinned at 60, ready climbs.
entries.command: for i in 1 2 3; do docker run -d --name caci-l8-node$i --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.orders --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 2 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 100000 --metrics-format compact; done

entries.label: Development Atom: 1 node × 2 consumers
entries.description: Same settings on one runtime: 2 consumers, ceiling 20, a backlog.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l8-node1 --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.orders --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 2 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 20000 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Stop the Lab 8 listeners
entries.description: ⚠ Removes caci-l8-node1..3; their unacked messages return to the queue.
entries.command: docker rm -f caci-l8-node1 caci-l8-node2 caci-l8-node3

entries.label: Lab 8 nack consumer
entries.description: caci-l8-nacker: deliver = redeliver, ack = 0 on boomi.poison.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l8-nacker --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.poison --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 1 --nack --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Single active consumer: queue and clients
entries.description: boomi.sac with x-single-active-consumer, a 50 msg/s feed and 3 × 1 consumers (stop other Lab 8 stand-ins first).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab declare queue --name boomi.sac --type quorum --durable true --arguments '{"x-single-active-consumer":true}'; docker run -d --name caci-l8-feed --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.sac --predeclared --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 50 --confirm 50 --flag persistent --metrics-format compact; for i in 1 2 3; do docker run -d --name caci-l8-node$i --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq --queue boomi.sac --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 1 --qos 10 --consumer-latency 5000 --metrics-format compact; done

entries.label: Last lines of a Lab 8 stand-in
entries.description: One-second rates printed by caci-l8-node1 (change the name).
entries.command: docker logs --tail 3 caci-l8-node1 2>&1

entries.label: Stop all Lab 8 stand-ins
entries.description: ⚠ Removes feed, listeners and nacker; the brokers stay.
entries.command: for c in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter name=caci-l8- | grep -v -- '-rmq'); do docker rm -f "$c"; done

entries.label: 3.13: nack loop
entries.description: On 3.13 every nack counts toward x-delivery-count.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-l8-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq313 --queue boomi.poison --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 1 --nack --time 8 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'receiving rate'

entries.label: Park poison messages
entries.description: One-off shovel orders.poison → orders.parking that deletes itself when the queue is empty (Lab 6).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl set_parameter shovel park-poison '{"src-protocol":"amqp091","src-uri":"amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1","src-queue":"orders.poison","dest-protocol":"amqp091","dest-uri":"amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmq1","dest-queue":"orders.parking","src-delete-after":"queue-length","ack-mode":"on-confirm"}'

entries.label: Runtime parameters
entries.description: Shovels (and other parameters) defined on the node; a finished one-off shovel is gone.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_parameters

entries.label: Export definitions for DR
entries.description: Everything except runtime parameters (no shovel copy) to lab06/primary-definitions.json.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab definitions export --stdout -t exclude_runtime_parameters > ../labs/files/lab06/primary-definitions.json

entries.label: Import definitions at the DR site
entries.description: Copies the file into caci-rmq-dr and imports it.
entries.command: docker cp ../labs/files/lab06/primary-definitions.json caci-rmq-dr:/tmp/primary-definitions.json && docker exec caci-rmq-dr rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab definitions import --file /tmp/primary-definitions.json

entries.label: DR site queues
entries.description: Name, type and depth at caci-rmq-dr.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq-dr rabbitmqctl list_queues -q name type messages

entries.label: Start the shovel to DR
entries.description: orders-to-dr from shovel-to-dr.json: dr-copy on the primary → orders.billing at DR, on-confirm.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl set_parameter shovel orders-to-dr "$(cat ../labs/files/lab06/shovel-to-dr.json)"

entries.label: Shovel status
entries.description: Name, type, state (running/starting/terminated), source and destination (passwords hidden).
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl shovel_status -q

entries.label: Replication lag (RPO)
entries.description: Primary dr-copy depth (not yet at DR) and the DR orders.billing depth.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl list_queues -q name messages | grep dr-copy; docker exec caci-rmq-dr rabbitmqctl list_queues -q name messages | grep -v dr-copy | grep billing

entries.label: Delete the shovel to DR
entries.description: ⚠ Stops replication to the DR site.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq1 rabbitmqctl clear_parameter shovel orders-to-dr

entries.label: DR drill: purge the DR queue
entries.description: ⚠ Empties orders.billing at the DR site before the drill.
entries.command: docker exec caci-rmq-dr rabbitmqadmin -u admin -p caci-lab purge queue --name orders.billing

entries.label: DR drill: producer only
entries.description: caci-producer: 500 msg/s into orders.events, no consumer at the primary.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-producer --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rabbitmq --exchange orders.events --type topic --routing-key order.us.created --predeclared --skip-binding-queues --queue orders.billing --producers 1 --consumers 0 --rate 500 --confirm 50 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: DR drill: lose the primary site
entries.description: ⚠ Kills all three primary nodes and the producer at once.
entries.command: docker kill caci-rmq1 caci-rmq2 caci-rmq3; docker rm -f caci-producer

entries.label: DR drill: consume at the DR site
entries.description: Two consumers drain orders.billing at caci-rmq-dr for 15 s.
entries.command: docker run --rm --network caci-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uri amqp://admin:caci-lab@rmqdr --queue orders.billing --predeclared --producers 0 --consumers 2 --qos 100 --time 15 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'receiving rate'

entries.label: DR drill: bring the primary back
entries.description: Starts rmq1..3 of the caci-lab project; the shovel resumes (and ships duplicates).
entries.command: docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab03/docker-compose.yml start rmq1 rmq2 rmq3

entries.label: Replay the DLQ (Lab 8)
entries.description: Self-deleting shovel boomi.dlq → boomi.orders, after the cause is fixed.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l8-rmq rabbitmqctl -q set_parameter shovel dlq-replay '{"src-protocol":"amqp091","src-uri":"amqp://","src-queue":"boomi.dlq","src-delete-after":"queue-length","dest-protocol":"amqp091","dest-uri":"amqp://","dest-queue":"boomi.orders"}'

entries.label: Blue and green queues side by side
entries.description: Depth and consumers of vhost integration on both Lab 7 clusters.
entries.command: echo '== blue (3.13)'; docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmqctl -q list_queues -p integration name type messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers; echo '== green (4.3)'; docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q list_queues -p integration name type messages_ready messages_unacknowledged consumers

entries.label: Blue: flow A consumer
entries.description: caci-l7-a-sub-blue: boomi-a on orders.billing, prefetch 50, all three blue nodes.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l7-a-sub-blue --network caci-l7-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uris amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue1/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue2/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue3/integration --queue orders.billing --predeclared --exchange orders.events --skip-binding-queues --metrics-format compact --producers 0 --consumers 1 --qos 50

entries.label: Blue: flow A producer
entries.description: caci-l7-a-pub-blue: 50 msg/s, key order.billing, confirms, persistent.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l7-a-pub-blue --network caci-l7-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uris amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue1/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue2/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@blue3/integration --queue orders.billing --predeclared --exchange orders.events --skip-binding-queues --metrics-format compact --producers 1 --consumers 0 --routing-key order.billing --rate 50 --confirm 10 --flag persistent

entries.label: Lab 7 stand-in rates
entries.description: Last 3 one-second lines of caci-l7-a-pub-blue: sent, confirmed, nacked (change the name).
entries.command: docker logs --tail 3 caci-l7-a-pub-blue 2>&1

entries.label: Lab 7 running stand-ins
entries.description: Which pub/sub/v2/shadow processes run, on which cluster.
entries.command: docker ps --filter name=caci-l7- --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E -- '-(pub|sub|v2|shadow)-' | sort

entries.label: Freeze flow A on blue
entries.description: ⚠ Stops the consumer, waits 10 s for a backlog, stops the producer.
entries.command: docker rm -f caci-l7-a-sub-blue; sleep 10; docker rm -f caci-l7-a-pub-blue

entries.label: Import blue's definitions as they are
entries.description: Refused on 4.3: ha-mode/ha-sync-mode are not recognised policy settings (partial import).
entries.command: docker exec -i caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl import_definitions < ../labs/files/lab07/blue-definitions.json

entries.label: Convert blue's definitions
entries.description: Drops mirroring and lazy mode, makes quorum queues, adds DLX and AE (Python in a container).
entries.command: docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$(cd ../labs/files/lab07 && pwd)":/w -w /w python:3.13-alpine python convert-definitions.py blue-definitions.json green-definitions.json

entries.label: Import the converted definitions
entries.description: Asynchronous import into green.
entries.command: docker exec -i caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl import_definitions < ../labs/files/lab07/green-definitions.json

entries.label: Move flow A's backlog to green
entries.description: Shovel move-a on green, on-confirm, deletes itself after the current queue length.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q set_parameter -p integration shovel move-a "$(cat ../labs/files/lab07/move-a.json)"

entries.label: Green: flow A producer and consumer
entries.description: Resumes flow A on green: producer first, then consumer.
entries.command: docker run -d --name caci-l7-a-pub-green --network caci-l7-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uris amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green1/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green2/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green3/integration --queue orders.billing --predeclared --exchange orders.events --skip-binding-queues --metrics-format compact --producers 1 --consumers 0 --routing-key order.billing --rate 50 --confirm 10 --flag persistent; docker run -d --name caci-l7-a-sub-green --network caci-l7-net pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 --uris amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green1/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green2/integration,amqp://boomi-a:caci-lab@green3/integration --queue orders.billing --predeclared --exchange orders.events --skip-binding-queues --metrics-format compact --producers 0 --consumers 1 --qos 50

entries.label: Capacity cap on green
entries.description: ⚠ Operator policy orders-cap: max-length 200 on orders.shipping (the failing wave).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q set_operator_policy -p integration orders-cap '^orders\.shipping$' '{"max-length":200}' --apply-to queues

entries.label: Bridge flow B live
entries.description: Shovel move-b on green (src-delete-after never) while clients switch.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q set_parameter -p integration shovel move-b "$(cat ../labs/files/lab07/move-b.json)"

entries.label: Green shovel status
entries.description: name, state and forwarded count of the bridges.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q shovel_status | cut -f1,4,16

entries.label: Remove the flow B bridge
entries.description: Clears move-b once blue's queue is empty.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q clear_parameter -p integration shovel move-b

entries.label: Roll back stranded messages
entries.description: Shovels green's orders.shipping and orders.dlq back to blue (both self-deleting).
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q set_parameter -p integration shovel back-shipping "$(cat ../labs/files/lab07/back-shipping.json)"; docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q set_parameter -p integration shovel back-dlq "$(cat ../labs/files/lab07/back-dlq.json)"

entries.label: Remove the capacity cap
entries.description: Clears operator policy orders-cap on green.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-green1 rabbitmqctl -q clear_operator_policy -p integration orders-cap

entries.label: Blue connections
entries.description: User and peer of every client still on blue: should be none before retiring it.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmqctl -q list_connections user peer_host

entries.label: Fence blue
entries.description: ⚠ max-connections 0 on blue's integration vhost: every stray client is refused.
entries.command: docker exec caci-l7-blue1 rabbitmqctl -q set_vhost_limits -p integration '{"max-connections": 0}'

entries.label: Lab URLs
entries.description: Where to point the browser.
entries.command: echo 'Grafana http://localhost:3000 (anonymous viewer; admin/caci-lab) | Prometheus http://localhost:9090/targets and /alerts | RabbitMQ UI http://localhost:15672 (admin/caci-lab)'

entries.label: Key node metrics
entries.description: Identity, alarms, unreachable peers, fds, disk and memory limit from rmq1's /metrics.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:15692/metrics | grep -E '^rabbitmq_(identity_info|alarms|unreachable|process_open_fds|disk_space_available_bytes|resident_memory_limit_bytes)'

entries.label: Per-object metrics
entries.description: One series per queue (expensive with thousands of queues).
entries.command: curl -s localhost:15692/metrics/per-object | grep '^rabbitmq_queue_messages_ready' | head

entries.label: Detailed metrics, chosen families
entries.description: Only queue_coarse_metrics and queue_consumer_count, as the alert rules scrape them.
entries.command: curl -s 'localhost:15692/metrics/detailed?family=queue_coarse_metrics&family=queue_consumer_count' | grep -E '^rabbitmq_detailed_queue_(messages_ready|consumers)' | head

entries.label: Prometheus targets
entries.description: Health of the six scrape targets (two jobs × three nodes).
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/targets | grep -oE '"scrapeUrl":"[^"]*"|"health":"[a-z]*"' | paste - - | sed 's/"scrapeUrl"://; s/"health"://'

entries.label: Alert rules loaded
entries.description: The RabbitMQ rule names (14 expected).
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/rules | grep -oE '"name":"RabbitMQ[A-Za-z]*"' | sort -u

entries.label: Active alerts
entries.description: Pending and firing alerts with their labels.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/alerts | grep -o '"alertname":"[^"]*","[^}]*' | cut -c1-120

entries.label: Firing alerts counted
entries.description: ALERTS{alertstate="firing"} by alert name.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}' | grep -o '"alertname":"[^"]*"' | sort | uniq -c

entries.label: PromQL: nodes up
entries.description: up{job="rabbitmq"} per instance: 1 up, 0 down.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=up{job="rabbitmq"}' | grep -oE '"instance":"[^"]*"|"value":\[[^]]*\]' | paste - -

entries.label: PromQL: ready messages per queue
entries.description: max by (queue) of rabbitmq_detailed_queue_messages_ready (leader's value).
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=max by (queue) (rabbitmq_detailed_queue_messages_ready)' | grep -oE '"queue":"[^"]*"\},"value":\[[^]]*\]'

entries.label: PromQL: backlog trend
entries.description: deriv over 1 m of lab.* queues: positive = growing, negative = draining.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=max by (queue) (deriv(rabbitmq_detailed_queue_messages_ready{queue=~"lab\\..*"}[1m]))' | grep -oE '"queue":"[^"]*"\},"value":\[[^]]*\]'

entries.label: PromQL: memory headroom
entries.description: Resident memory as a fraction of the memory limit, per node.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:9090/api/v1/query --data-urlencode 'query=rabbitmq_process_resident_memory_bytes / rabbitmq_resident_memory_limit_bytes' | grep -oE '"instance":"[^"]*"|"value":\[[^]]*\]' | paste - -

entries.label: Reload Prometheus rules
entries.description: After editing prometheus/rabbitmq-alerts.yml (lifecycle API is enabled).
entries.command: curl -s -X POST localhost:9090/-/reload && echo reloaded

entries.label: Grafana health and dashboards
entries.description: API health, then the provisioned dashboard titles.
entries.command: curl -s localhost:3000/api/health; echo; curl -s -u admin:caci-lab 'localhost:3000/api/search?type=dash-db' | grep -oE '"title":"[^"]*"'

entries.label: Nodes and AHV zones
entries.description: Five nodes; workers carry topology.kubernetes.io/zone.
entries.command: kubectl get nodes -L topology.kubernetes.io/zone

entries.label: RabbitMQ CRDs
entries.description: Cluster Operator and Topology Operator resource types.
entries.command: kubectl get crd | grep rabbitmq.com

entries.label: Operators running
entries.description: cert-manager and rabbitmq-system deployments.
entries.command: kubectl get deploy -n cert-manager; kubectl get deploy -n rabbitmq-system

entries.label: Cluster, pods and services
entries.description: RabbitmqCluster, StatefulSet, pods with nodes, Services and PVCs.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get rabbitmqclusters,statefulset,pods,svc,pvc -o wide

entries.label: Pod placement by AHV host
entries.description: Pod, status, Kubernetes node and zone.
entries.command: bash ../labs/files/lab04/show-placement.sh messaging

entries.label: Cluster status inside a pod
entries.description: Running nodes as rabbit@caci-rabbit-server-N.caci-rabbit-nodes.messaging.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- rabbitmqctl cluster_status | sed -n '/Running Nodes/,/Versions/p'

entries.label: Operator-generated configuration
entries.description: conf.d files and the operator defaults (peer discovery, disk limit).
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- sh -c 'ls /etc/rabbitmq/conf.d/; cat /etc/rabbitmq/conf.d/10-operatorDefaults.conf /etc/rabbitmq/conf.d/90-userDefinedConfiguration.conf'

entries.label: Memory watermark from the pod limit
entries.description: The log line computed from total_memory_available_override_value.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging logs caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq | grep 'Memory high watermark set'

entries.label: preStop hook and grace period
entries.description: await_online_quorum_plus_one + drain, and terminationGracePeriodSeconds 604800.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get sts caci-rabbit-server -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].lifecycle.preStop.exec.command[2]}{"\n"}{.spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds}{"\n"}'

entries.label: PodDisruptionBudget
entries.description: MAX UNAVAILABLE 1; ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS 1 when all pods are ready.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get pdb caci-rabbit

entries.label: Topology objects
entries.description: Every Topology Operator object with its Ready condition (use full resource names).
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get vhosts.rabbitmq.com,exchanges.rabbitmq.com,queues.rabbitmq.com,bindings.rabbitmq.com,policies.rabbitmq.com,users.rabbitmq.com,permissions.rabbitmq.com -o 'custom-columns=KIND:.kind,NAME:.metadata.name,READY:.status.conditions[0].status'

entries.label: Why a topology object is not ready
entries.description: Events and status of Queue orders-billing.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging describe queues.rabbitmq.com orders-billing

entries.label: Queues on the broker
entries.description: orders.billing quorum with policy orders-limits, plus leader and online members.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- rabbitmqctl -q list_queues -p integration name type policy leader members online

entries.label: Default user credentials
entries.description: Username and password the operator generated, for the UI.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get secret caci-rabbit-default-user -o jsonpath='{.data.username}' | base64 -d; echo; kubectl -n messaging get secret caci-rabbit-default-user -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d; echo

entries.label: Port-forward the UI
entries.description: http://localhost:15680; stop with Ctrl+C.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging port-forward svc/caci-rabbit 15680:15672

entries.label: Traffic as boomi-orders
entries.description: One-shot PerfTest pod through Service caci-rabbit: about 500 msg/s for 20 s.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging run caci-perf --rm -i --restart=Never --image=pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 -- --uri "amqp://boomi-orders:Orders-Lab-2026@caci-rabbit.messaging.svc:5672/integration" --exchange orders.events --type topic --routing-key order.us.created --predeclared --skip-binding-queues --queue orders.billing --producers 1 --consumers 1 --qos 50 --confirm 100 --rate 500 --time 20 --metrics-format compact 2>&1 | grep 'rate avg'

entries.label: Health checks inside a pod
entries.description: Local alarms and quorum-critical check on caci-rabbit-server-0 before a drain.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- rabbitmq-diagnostics -q check_local_alarms && kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- rabbitmq-queues check_if_node_is_quorum_critical

entries.label: Lose a pod
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes caci-rabbit-server-1; it returns with the same name, node and PVC.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging delete pod caci-rabbit-server-1 --wait=false

entries.label: Watch pods
entries.description: Terminating, Init, Running 0/1, 1/1; stop with Ctrl+C.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging get pods -o wide -w

entries.label: Volumes pinned to nodes
entries.description: Each kind PV is a directory on one node, so its pod comes back there.
entries.command: kubectl get pv -o custom-columns='PV:.metadata.name,CLAIM:.spec.claimRef.name,NODE:.spec.nodeAffinity.required.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0].values[0]'

entries.label: Export NODE (server-0's node)
entries.description: Sets $NODE in this shell for the cordon, drain and uncordon entries.
entries.command: export NODE=$(kubectl -n messaging get pod caci-rabbit-server-0 -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}'); echo $NODE

entries.label: Cordon and drain $NODE
entries.description: ⚠ Evicts caci-rabbit-server-0 (its preStop hook drains RabbitMQ); needs NODE exported.
entries.command: kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=600s

entries.label: Export NODE2 and try a second drain
entries.description: ⚠ Sets $NODE2 (server-1's node) and drains it: the PDB refuses until the 30 s timeout.
entries.command: export NODE2=$(kubectl -n messaging get pod caci-rabbit-server-1 -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}'); kubectl drain $NODE2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=30s

entries.label: Uncordon both nodes
entries.description: Releases $NODE2 and $NODE, then waits for server-0 to be ready.
entries.command: kubectl uncordon $NODE2 $NODE && kubectl -n messaging wait --for=condition=Ready pod/caci-rabbit-server-0 --timeout=300s

entries.label: Rebalance inside the cluster
entries.description: Spreads quorum leaders after pods come back.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging exec caci-rabbit-server-0 -c rabbitmq -- rabbitmq-queues rebalance quorum

entries.label: Background load for a rolling restart
entries.description: caci-load pod: 200 msg/s for 400 s through Service caci-rabbit.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging run caci-load --restart=Never --image=pivotalrabbitmq/perf-test:2.25.0 -- --uri "amqp://boomi-orders:Orders-Lab-2026@caci-rabbit.messaging.svc:5672/integration" --exchange orders.events --type topic --routing-key order.us.created --predeclared --skip-binding-queues --queue orders.billing --producers 1 --consumers 1 --qos 50 --confirm 100 --rate 200 --time 400 --metrics-format compact

entries.label: Rolling restart
entries.description: ⚠ Restarts every RabbitMQ pod, highest ordinal first, one at a time.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging rollout restart statefulset caci-rabbit-server && kubectl -n messaging rollout status statefulset caci-rabbit-server --timeout=900s

entries.label: Seconds where traffic dipped
entries.description: caci-load lines below 150 msg/s sent, then removes the pod.
entries.command: kubectl -n messaging logs caci-load | grep 'msg/s' | awk '$3+0 < 150 {print $2, "sent", $3, "received", $9}'; kubectl -n messaging delete pod caci-load

entries.label: Cluster Operator logs
entries.description: Last reconcile messages of rabbitmq-cluster-operator.
entries.command: kubectl -n rabbitmq-system logs deploy/rabbitmq-cluster-operator --tail=20

entries.label: Topology Operator logs
entries.description: Last messages of messaging-topology-operator.
entries.command: kubectl -n rabbitmq-system logs deploy/messaging-topology-operator --tail=20

entries.label: Placement demo
entries.description: Naive (per node) vs host-aware (per AHV host) pause Deployments.
entries.command: kubectl create namespace placement-demo; kubectl apply -f ../labs/files/lab04/placement-demo.yaml; sleep 15; bash ../labs/files/lab04/show-placement.sh placement-demo

entries.label: Ask host-aware for a fourth pod
entries.description: Three AHV hosts, four replicas: one pod stays Pending; prints the FailedScheduling reason.
entries.command: kubectl -n placement-demo scale deploy host-aware --replicas=4; sleep 8; kubectl -n placement-demo get events --field-selector reason=FailedScheduling -o jsonpath='{.items[-1].message}{"\n"}'

entries.label: Remove the placement demo
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes namespace placement-demo.
entries.command: kubectl delete namespace placement-demo

entries.label: Remove leftover stand-ins
entries.description: ⚠ Deletes PerfTest stand-ins from Labs 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 (brokers stay).
entries.command: for c in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -E '^caci-(pt-bg|backlog|l5-|traffic|producer|poison|l7-[abc]-|l8-(feed|node|nacker))'); do docker rm -f "$c"; done

entries.label: Lab 1/2 cleanup
entries.description: ⚠ Removes the single node, its volume and the exported definitions.
entries.command: docker rm -f caci-pt-bg 2>/dev/null; docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab01/docker-compose.yml down -v; rm -f ../labs/files/lab01/integration-definitions.json

entries.label: Lab 3/5/6 cleanup
entries.description: ⚠ Removes cluster, DR site, Prometheus, Grafana, volumes and exported definitions.
entries.command: docker rm -f caci-backlog caci-l5-batch-sub caci-l5-batch-pub caci-l5-nocons caci-l5-slow caci-traffic caci-producer caci-poison 2>/dev/null; docker compose -f ../labs/files/lab06/docker-compose.yml down -v --remove-orphans; rm -f ../labs/files/lab06/primary-definitions.json

entries.label: Remove the kind network
entries.description: After deleting caci-k8s: kind leaves its kind network behind.
entries.command: docker network rm kind

entries.label: Remove caci- containers and volumes
entries.description: ⚠ Every caci- container (not the kind nodes) with its anonymous volumes.
entries.command: for c in $(docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}' --filter name=caci- | grep -v '^caci-k8s-'); do docker rm -fv "$c"; done

entries.label: Remove caci- networks and volumes
entries.description: ⚠ Leftover caci-net, caci-l7-net, caci-l8-net and any caci- named volume.
entries.command: for n in $(docker network ls -q --filter name=caci-); do docker network rm "$n"; done; for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter name=caci-); do docker volume rm "$v"; done

entries.label: Verify nothing is left
entries.description: No caci- containers, networks or volumes, and no caci-k8s kind cluster.
entries.command: docker ps -a --filter name=caci- --format '{{.Names}}'; docker network ls --filter name=caci- --format '{{.Name}}'; docker volume ls --filter name=caci- --format '{{.Name}}'; kind get clusters
